rfm_tuples.R: Delinquencies greater than 90 days across our residential investor bridge loans increased to 6.7% at December 31, 2024 from 4.4% at December 31, 2023. This increase was predominantly driven by the 2022 vintage portfolio... we continue to manage through pockets of stress, largely with a handful of more significant borrower relationships where a combination of rate modifications, maturity extensions and fresh equity has been utilized.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: re-derive the implied workout intensity. If the 90+ DQ rate is 6.7%, what is the cumulative modification/extension activity for the year? Anything that pushes modified+extended >> reported DQ rate suggests reported delinquency UNDERSTATES distress.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (cross-section of 10-K MD&A risk factor disclosures)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Same 10-K (Risk Factor, p.~17): during 2024, residential investor bridge loans with cumulative UPB ~$663M were rate-modified (with interest deferrals + fresh capital), AND ~$402M had maturity extensions. Bridge book FV at YE24 = $1.94B. So $663M + $402M = ~$1.07B of activity, ~55% of bridge book (gross UPB basis materially similar). Per-Q1-2025 10-Q: total non-accrual UPB $342M (17.5% of $1.94B bridge book) with $77M of FV writedown already taken. 'Modified or put into forbearance' UPB was $206M in Q1-2025 (~10% of book in one quarter).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Headline 6.7% 90+ DQ materially understates economic distress: real workout exposure spans roughly half the bridge book by UPB when modifications, rate cuts with interest deferral, maturity extensions, and full non-accrual are aggregated. Mode-B derivation flags that current-period stress flows are large relative to reported DQ stocks, consistent with continued FV markdowns in 2025-2026 quarters.

Q1 also shows fair value of bridge book dropped from $1.94B to $1.88B (-$60M) on top of $77M of writedowns already at YE24.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Claim drift in the direction of tighter concentration: management now identifies just two sponsors as the primary drivers. This means RWT bridge-portfolio losses going forward are largely binary on outcomes for two specific borrowers — under-disclosed name-level concentration that the headline 6.7% DQ rate does not convey.

rfm_tuples.M_value: 12-month obligations as of Dec 31 2024: $124M exchangeable notes maturing Oct 2025; up to $397M of bridge-loan fund-up commitments; plus interest on $880M of corporate debt at 7.75%-9.125% coupons; plus dividends ~$89M/yr common + $7M preferred. Sources: $245M unrestricted cash + estimated $200M from financing the $325M unencumbered assets = ~$445M before any operating cash. RWT explicitly states 'we may repay (all or in part) with the proceeds of new unsecured debt... at significantly higher interest rates than the maturing borrowings.' Already issued $145M senior + $40M convert in 2024 at 9.0-9.125% / 7.75% coupons, $4.6B equity market cap-only ~132M shares outstanding × ~$6.50.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Liquidity claim is reasonable but only because it is contingent on continued capital-markets access. Cost of new debt is ~9% vs. blended portfolio yields that have compressed; this is a slow-bleed-on-NIM story, not an insolvency story. The disclosure does not quantify how dependent the 12-month plan is on issuing fresh equity/debt — Mode-B audit reveals at least $124M needs refi within 12 months.

Net: Q1-2025 still booked a $5M FV LOSS despite spread tightening — the bridge book is cancelling out the securities-book recovery.

summary: RWT is a 30-year mortgage REIT with clean governance signals: long-tenure auditor (Grant Thornton, 2005-) issued unqualified opinions on both financials and ICFR; no Item 9 disagreements; no material weakness; no insider selling beyond a single $90K CLO transaction in 18 months; covenant compliance asserted and consistent across the 10-K and the May-2025 10-Q. The honesty-alpha framework's strongest contribution here is therefore EXCLUSION-as-a-positive: there is no evidence of obscured distress at the corporate level. However, Mode-B analysis of the residential investor bridge book reveals a meaningful disclosure gap: the headline 6.7% 90+ delinquency rate is supported by an iceberg of ~$663M of rate-modified-with-interest-deferral loans plus ~$402M of maturity-extended loans (combined ~55% of bridge UPB), and the Q1-2025 10-Q narrowed the concentration description from 'a handful of borrowers' to 'two sponsor relationships' driving incremental Q1 delinquency. Bridge book FV continued to bleed in Q1-2025 even with spread tightening, offsetting securities-book gains. Pre-cutoff drawdown of -19.2% appears to be the market pricing this slow-bleed plus 9%-coupon refi cost on $124M of 2025 maturities, not a deception story.
